While it can cause bone deformities, it does not explain the specific metabolic abnormalities (hypophosphatemia, elevated 1,25-D, low PTH, undetectable FGF23, hypercalciuria) seen in this patient.
X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH) is characterized by elevated FGF23, which is undetectable in this patient. It also typically presents with normal or low 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, not elevated.

While 1,25-D is high, the overall clinical picture and other lab values (low PTH, undetectable FGF23) do not fit perfectly, and the reference diagnosis is more specific.
